completed_scope: Canonical 404 permits bounded descriptor URL fallback for index children, config/layers, weak subjects and source-referrer descriptors. Other canonical failures do not start fallback.

Every locator uses only the most-specific approved source credential and explicit signed-query permission. Common address/network/query/hop limits and HTTPS downgrade rejection remain; unapproved candidates make no HTTP request.

Verify descriptor digest/size and manifest media/structure before complete graph publication. Missing/temporary alternates can advance; authorization, transport, integrity and resource failures cannot become successful stale or partial publication.

Combine unique locators for duplicate child descriptors. Recover direct digest locators after restart from bounded canonical parents whose raw CAS bytes are verified/reparsed; normalized descriptor identities must match.

For alternate-only referents, derive the subject from verified cached bytes and rewalk the complete current source referrers index or 404-only legacy fallback. Newly issued signed advertisements work after process restart without durable URL bindings.

Current direct digest denial is checked before cache/source selection. Denials during intake retain explicit error classification after fenced failure cleanup. Current grants, tenant RLS, graph policy and member/publication fences remain.

Original immutable manifest bytes retain publisher-supplied descriptor fields exactly. Parsed URL fields are transient; normalized metadata/cache/journal/jobs do not copy locator queries or source credentials.

Actual native server/ORAS tests prove proxy/group exact layouts, duplicate locators, restart and direct member refresh, rotated referrer queries, corruption rollback, valid recovery, current denial and normalized durable secrecy.
Previous native clients and one pinned real Docker Hub/anonymous-token/CloudFront journey pass against matching exact clean binaries.

first_failures.cause: Approved descriptor URLs were discarded, so canonical blob absence failed the graph.
Forced direct digest denial lost its explicit 403 response through failed retrieval classification; this failure did not prove denied bytes were served.

limits: All 450 broad capabilities and 41 format families remain open; no broad readiness verdict is positive.
New actual native server process tests use the production binary, while Go store/server/test runners also run under the race detector. This is not native Linux/Windows or container packaging proof.

Owned alternate sources are HTTP loopback fixtures. The separate real HTTPS provider proof is one pinned Linux arm64 Docker Hub/anonymous-token/CloudFront image; other providers/private credentials/PKI/client/platform combinations remain required.

Publisher-supplied URLs remain in exact original manifest bytes. Expired immutable signed URLs need usable alternates/source repair or a newly published manifest; no package signature or scanner assessment is inferred.

Full source lifecycle/removal/delete/restore, source/locator/grant races, mutation/fault/scale campaigns, graph-budget configuration, migration/recovery/HA, fair workers, scanner/S3/console and every remaining product stage remain required.
